h1: Powder Coating by Industry: Durable Finishes for Ontario Businesses

blocks.text: Powder coating by industry means choosing the coating, preparation and checks that suit the sector using the part, not just the metal underneath. Koojo Custom Powder Coating, based in Ontario, applies this approach for seven sectors as a trusted industrial coating partner and B2B powder coating shop. Pick your sector below, or send photos and drawings through the [quote form](/get-a-quote) for a clear plan. Each sector page explains typical parts, finishes and checks.

blocks.text: Industries We Serve

We serve seven sectors: fabrication, manufacturing, machine shops, construction, food processing, agriculture and public institutions. Powder coating by industry gives each one preparation and a finish suited to its parts, so a bracket for a plant floor and a gate for a church are treated differently. Select a sector to see typical parts and recommended finishes.

items.title: Metal Fabricators and Welding Shops
items.text: Brackets, frames, tanks and structural assemblies need welded assembly finishing that covers seams evenly. We handle weld spatter removal before pretreatment, so Ontario metal fabricators receive fabricated steel parts ready to install. Send drawings and part counts for a quick plan. Related project: Automation Line Frame.

items.title: Manufacturing and Automation
items.text: Conveyor frames, machine guards and enclosures must match in colour and still fit after coating. Our OEM finishing programs cover equipment frame finishing in controlled batches, with colour and powder traceability records for reorders. Parts are checked for fit after coating so assembly goes smoothly. Related projects: Conveyor Frame for an Automotive Plant and Robotic Base.

items.title: Machine Shops
items.text: Machined components need protection without changing tolerances. We use masking for tight-tolerance parts, and masking and plugging for threads and bores, in small batches or single prototypes. Threaded features stay clean, and one-off parts are welcome. See more finished work in our portfolio.

items.title: Contractors and Construction
items.text: Handrails, stair components and structural steel must arrive on schedule and survive the weather. We offer jobsite delivery coordination and outdoor metalwork finishes cured for UV, rain and road salt, and delivery can be timed to your site schedule. Related project: Safety Bollards.

items.title: Food Processing Equipment
items.text: Line frames, supports and guards face constant washing. Cleaning-tolerant coatings resist flaking where moisture is steady, and we discuss food-contact powder options for surfaces near product. We record the powder used so your quality team has documentation. Related project: Food Processing Line Frame.

items.title: Agricultural and Heavy Equipment
items.text: Implements, trailers and attachments face mud, fertilizer and sun. We clean older equipment to bare metal and apply a tough finish for rust prevention for equipment, including heavy steel fabrications. Parts return ready to work, and heavy items are discussed at quoting. Browse related work in our portfolio.

items.title: Municipal and Institutional
items.text: Bollards, gates and railings must stay safe and presentable for years. Our institutional metalwork finishing covers public space metalwork, with scratch-hiding textures that suit busy sites. Documented checks are available with your quote. Related project: Church Gates.

blocks.text: Powder Coating by Industry at a Glance
This table summarizes how finish needs change from one sector to the next.
How We Match a Finish to Your Sector

We match a finish to your sector in four steps: review, prepare, apply and cure, then inspect. Because powder coating by industry depends on how each part is used, every step is adjusted to the sector instead of following one fixed recipe.

items: Review. We ask where the part will be used, how it is cleaned and which surfaces must stay bare. Photos, drawings and part counts help us give an accurate plan. Early review prevents rework and surprise costs.

Prepare. Pretreatment before coating drives adhesion and corrosion protection for steel. Depending on the metal, we degrease, treat, remove rust, then finish with careful masking. Skipping this stage is the most common reason coatings fail early.

Apply and cure. Electrostatic powder application wraps thermoset powder evenly around the part, which then enters the curing oven at roughly 180–200 °C. Our load capacity is up to 6,000 lb; see [capabilities](/capabilities). Heavy parts need longer oven time to reach temperature all the way through.
Inspect. We check coverage, appearance and film thickness before release, then pack parts to protect the finish. Any part that misses the standard is corrected before release.

blocks.text: Quality and Certification

Our quality process is certified through the Absolute Bureau of Certification. We check adhesion against ASTM D3359 adhesion methods, measure dry film thickness following ASTM D7091, and treat ASTM B117 results as a reference for salt spray resistance. Test reports on request and quality assurance documentation are available for audited customers. These checks apply to every sector, and the depth of documentation depends on what your buyer or auditor requires. Ask for the reports you need when you request a quote, so they are prepared with the job instead of after it. Details are on our [certification page](/certification).
Don't See Your Industry?

Other sectors are welcome. We often coat HVAC and ductwork, playground and park equipment and church gates and religious metalwork. For one-off pieces, prototypes and art, see specialty and custom projects, or send photos and we will say honestly whether powder coating is the right fit. We also review parts that arrive with old paint or rust and explain what preparation is realistic. Tell us the metal, size and use, and we will reply with a straight answer.
Turnaround, Hours and Delivery Times
Planning around times keeps production moving. Times depend on part size, preparation and shop load, so we confirm a date when we quote rather than promise one in advance.

Frequently Asked Questions

blocks.q: How do I know which finish suits my sector?
blocks.a: Start with where the part will be used and how it is cleaned. Outdoor parts need weather-stable powders and machined parts need careful masking. Send us the details and we will recommend durable metal coatings before you commit. Photos of the part and a note on its environment make that recommendation faster and more accurate.

blocks.q: Can one order include parts for different sectors?
blocks.a: Yes. Each part is prepared and coated to its own requirement, and we note the specification on the job so records stay clear. This keeps mixed orders organized and prevents a finish meant for one use from being applied to another.

blocks.q: Do you handle repeat production runs?
blocks.a: Yes. We keep powder and colour details on file, so later runs match earlier ones and keep batch consistency across orders. Standing schedules can be arranged with your planner. Tell us your usual volumes and delivery dates so we can plan oven time ahead.

blocks.q: Can you coat parts that will touch food?
blocks.a: We can discuss suitable powders for surfaces near product. The right choice depends on the part and your compliance rules, so share your requirement with your quote request. We will document the powder used so your quality team has a record for audits.

blocks.q: How does the sector affect my quote?
blocks.a: The sector decides preparation, masking, finish and paperwork, which drive the price. Send photos, quantity, size, metal and exposure, and we will explain the basis of the price. The more detail you share, the fewer assumptions we need to make.
